text:
Los Angeles is 5-7-2, and it's hard to find the part of the game that's broken. The Kings take 50% of the expected goals, score almost exactly what their chances deserve (43 goals on 43.6 expected), and have allowed about four more than the shots against would predict. Our numbers have them three points behind where their play should have them. That's a goaltending gap more than a hockey one, and it's early enough to close.

The headline is Artemi Panarin, already looking at home on a line with Adrian Kempe. With Alex Laferriere on the right side, that trio has outscored teams 8-1 at five on five and made 4.0 expected goals per hour. With Quinton Byfield instead, the chances were even better (65%) and the goals went the other way, 5-1 against. Same players, very different luck.

On the blue line, Erik Gustafsson and Brandt Clarke are driving play at 62%. Clarke took a hit from Ottawa's Hayden Hodgson that drew a two-game suspension, per The Athletic's Julian McKenzie. Brian Dumoulin and Mikey Anderson sit at 46%.

A 3-2 loss to Buffalo, part of the Sabres' perfect California trip, didn't help. Still, 45% playoff odds on an 88-point pace is a team that's one good goaltending month from looking fine. Darcy Kuemper is the name to watch.
headline: The Kings are waiting for their goalies to catch up
